content:
maria (Product Designer): hey team — opened a quick design sync for the private setup prereq step. trying a compact status strip instead of full accordions so users see a single scan summary first. feedback? https://figma.com/file/yyy

deen (UX Writer): nice direction. question: what exact wording lives in the strip? should be short and action-oriented.

maria (Product Designer): thinking three status chips in a horizontal strip: Network · Agent · Keys. each chip shows short state + count e.g. "Network: 1 issue" or "Agent: all good". clicking expands inline details.

ravi (Platform Eng): implementation note: expansion should not rerun checks. just reveal cached results and a single recommended command to run locally. also prefer progressive disclosure for logs.

frank (QA): prefer chips to be keyboard-focusable and have an explicit "expand" affordance. testers get confused when click targets are small.

a11y-bot: accessibility checks: chips must be buttons with clear accessible name (e.g., aria-label="Network checks: 3 passed, 1 requires attention"). If counts change, update an aria-live region. Avoid using color alone to indicate status.

dean (UX Writer): copy options proposal — short forms to try:
- Success: "All clear"
- Warning: "Action suggested"
- Error: "Action required"
- Empty: "Not checked"
Which feels more helpful than "passing/failing"?

maria (Product Designer): i like "All clear" and "Action required". "Action suggested" is softer for intermittent issues.

ravi (Platform Eng): for network failures please surface a single prioritized remediation: e.g., "Open port 5432 from your gateway" plus a one-line command folks can copy. we should also include a link to KB with exact steps per cloud vendor.

frank (QA): also let's add deterministic test IDs to each check so QA can reference them. small JSON blob in the expanded panel with {check_id, last_run, code_snippet}.

a11y-bot: for the expanded details use <pre> for code snippets and ensure there's a "Copy" button with aria-label="Copy command for network diagnose". When the copy happens, update aria-live with "Copied to clipboard".

dean (UX Writer): microcopy tweak for KB links: use explicit CTAs: "See troubleshooting steps" instead of just "Learn more". helps with scanning.

maria (Product Designer): good. another UX question: default view should show all chips collapsed, but an opt-in toggle "Show only issues" would hide the green ones. thoughts?

ravi (Platform Eng): server-side we can add a query param to the checks endpoint to return only failing ones. but be careful: toggles must be discoverable and persist across reloads.

frank (QA): testing note: when toggling between views, ensure focus does not jump unexpectedly. focus should stay on the toggle. Also test with screen readers that only-visible content is announced appropriately.

a11y-bot: recommendation: implement the toggle as a checkbox input with role=switch and clear label. Persist preference in localStorage and announce via aria-live when the filter is applied: "Filter applied: showing issues only".

dean (UX Writer): suggested sentences for the expanded failure row:
- Title: "Port 5432 unreachable"
- Short: "Your database port is blocked from the CIDR range you provided."
- Action CTA: "Open port on firewall (copy command)"
- KB link: "See troubleshooting steps for firewall rules"
Keep it under 140 chars.

maria (Product Designer): love that. let's keep the language direct and avoid jargon.

ravi (Platform Eng): propose a single-line diagnose command example for copy:
```
# run from a bastion with your CIDR
nc -vz 10.0.1.12 5432
```
Include a fallback curl check for HTTP-based services.

frank (QA): QA will validate behavior on desktop, tablet, mobile. mobile note: convert the strip into stacked cards and make the whole card tappable to expand. ensure touch target >= 44px.

a11y-bot: interactive patterns to confirm: keyboard only (tab/enter/space), screen reader (NVDA/VoiceOver), and high contrast mode. Post axe results in thread.

dean (UX Writer): small phrasing alternative for the chip summary: "2 checks, 1 issue" vs "1 issue out of 3" 12 which is clearer?

maria (Product Designer): i'd go with "1 issue out of 3" 12 more explicit about scope.

ravi (Platform Eng): logging policy: do not show raw secrets in expanded logs. redact any sensitive headers or tokens. we should surface a safe diagnostic id that support can request.

frank (QA): capturing acceptance criteria: chips present and keyboard-focusable; expanded details show one copyable command, KB link, and redacted logs; toggle for showing issues only; responsive stack on narrow screens; aria-live announcements for dynamic changes.

maria (Product Designer): owners: ravi implements backend filtering + redact rules, kai will do frontend prototype (i'll tag kai in ticket), deen to finalize microcopy, frank to draft QA plan, a11y-bot to run axe on prototype. target: PR by next Tue.

a11y-bot: reminder: add role="status" to ephemeral update messages for automatic SR announcement.

dean (UX Writer): i'll drop final copy into the figma file and leave alternative phrasings in comments.

maria (Product Designer): thanks all 12 will post updated link and ping once prototype is up.
